generated_examples.rule: Each source becomes one research-only example. No parcel heritage designation, consent, archaeological conclusion, setting harm, Heritage at Risk opportunity or Future Growth score is inferred.

second_pass_examples.rule: Recheck designation type, legal extent, curtilage, consent regime, COI/BPN temporal effect and separate planning/LBC/SMC/wreck-licence states before any promotion.

third_pass_examples.rule: Recheck current NHLE/LPA/HER source, collector versus underlying-data freshness, annual Heritage at Risk snapshot, mixed provenance, amendments, expiry and supersession.

fourth_pass_examples.rule: Recheck point/outline/map evidence against exact legal list entry, full-scale map, current conservation appraisal, HER event/source data, field evaluation, setting/significance and proposal-specific impact. Geographic proximity alone is never promoted.

extra_examples.fact: Historic England's open-data page reports core NHLE GIS layers updated 20 July 2026.
extra_examples.gate: Use current GIS for screening but re-open the exact legal list entry when making a parcel conclusion.

extra_examples.fact: Historic England states the map in a list entry is for quick reference and may not be to scale.
extra_examples.gate: Do not derive legal boundary/curtilage from screen-map pixels or approximate point positions.

extra_examples.fact: Planning Data explicitly says its listed-building dataset shows a point within the building and not the listing extent.
extra_examples.gate: A point intersection or distance cannot determine whether the target parcel is within listed curtilage.

extra_examples.fact: The outline dataset is incomplete and does not consistently show listed-building curtilage.
extra_examples.gate: Never promote or reject a parcel solely from this outline layer; verify legal scope and site facts.

extra_examples.fact: Alterations affecting special interest may require Listed Building Consent from the LPA.
extra_examples.gate: Planning permission does not imply LBC, and LBC does not imply planning permission where both are needed.

extra_examples.fact: Historic England states SMC can coexist with planning, building-regulation and ecological requirements.
extra_examples.gate: Granted SMC must not be stored as a complete all-consents-ready state.

extra_examples.fact: SMC can be granted subject to conditions that must be complied with before/during works.
extra_examples.gate: Consent granted is distinct from pre-commencement conditions satisfied.

extra_examples.ref: Registered battlefield no separate consent gate
extra_examples.fact: Historic England states registered battlefields do not have their own separate consent regime.
extra_examples.gate: Do not invent a battlefield-consent state; assess through planning policy/significance and any separate archaeology controls.

extra_examples.fact: Certain diving, salvage, interference and deposits within protected wreck restricted areas require a licence.
extra_examples.gate: Presence inside the protected area does not describe whether the proposed activity is licensed or exempt/permitted.

extra_examples.fact: Historic England assesses licence applications and may recommend conditions.
extra_examples.gate: Application submitted or advice received is not licence granted.

extra_examples.fact: A Building Preservation Notice can temporarily protect a building for up to six months.
extra_examples.gate: Check live dates; an expired BPN must not be treated as current protection unless listing/another control superseded it.

extra_examples.fact: A granted Certificate of Immunity prevents listing/BPN for five years for the relevant building.
extra_examples.gate: COI expiry and exact covered building are required; a COI does not remove conservation-area, scheduled-monument or other controls.

extra_examples.fact: Planning Data's BPN dataset is limited and MHCLG-created pending authoritative LPA data publication.
extra_examples.gate: No BPN platform hit cannot be converted into no active BPN.

extra_examples.fact: Planning Data describes the national conservation-area dataset as incomplete and containing duplicates.
extra_examples.gate: Resolve the current LPA designation map/document before parcel scoring.

extra_examples.fact: Conservation-area designation protects special character/appearance through planning management.
extra_examples.gate: Overlap is not automatic refusal; assess proposal-specific effect on the identified character and appearance.

extra_examples.fact: Historic England distinguishes appraisal of significance/character from management proposals.
extra_examples.gate: Use the current relevant documents and do not treat an old appraisal as the whole present policy/management position.

extra_examples.fact: Planning Data indexes conservation-area documents from multiple providers with mixed provenance.
extra_examples.gate: Choose the live LPA appraisal/designation/management document by date and authority, not the first indexed document.

extra_examples.fact: HERs contain monuments, events, sources and archaeological information used in planning.
extra_examples.gate: A HER search is not a substitute for field evaluation where planning evidence requires intrusive or non-intrusive investigation.

extra_examples.ref: No HER hit versus no archaeology
extra_examples.fact: HERs are dynamic information services containing known records and events.
extra_examples.gate: No HER record must not be treated as proof of no archaeology; unknown remains may exist.

extra_examples.fact: APA tiers express archaeological sensitivity/risk based on existing information.
extra_examples.gate: Risk tier is not confirmation of an archaeological asset at the exact development footprint.

extra_examples.fact: Historic England explains low risk is not negligible risk and discoveries can still occur.
extra_examples.gate: Do not convert low APA sensitivity into no archaeology.

extra_examples.fact: Current GLAAS project guidance sets expected archaeological methods by site type.
extra_examples.gate: A written scheme/standard does not prove investigation, archive or publication has been completed.

extra_examples.fact: Heritage statements provide proportionate significance and impact information.
extra_examples.gate: Submission of a statement does not mean the LPA/Historic England agrees with its conclusions.

extra_examples.fact: Decision-taking guidance requires understanding significance and the proposal's effect.
extra_examples.gate: Designation grade/category alone cannot determine harm level or planning balance.

extra_examples.fact: Historic England is expert adviser while statutory decision-makers determine applications in most cases.
extra_examples.gate: Advice/consultation response is not the final LPA/Secretary of State decision unless the specific regime provides otherwise.

extra_examples.fact: The battlefield dataset shows a July 2026 collector run but newest underlying data found in February 2025.
extra_examples.gate: Never equate collector freshness with underlying designation freshness.

extra_examples.ref: World Heritage dataset versus UNESCO definitive list
extra_examples.fact: Planning Data notes UNESCO holds the definitive World Heritage list.
extra_examples.gate: Use Planning Data as screening/context and confirm authoritative WHS status/management evidence.

extra_examples.fact: Planning Data currently contains only a subset of World Heritage buffer-zone records.
extra_examples.gate: No platform buffer hit cannot prove no setting/buffer implications.

extra_examples.ref: Heritage at Risk annual snapshot gate
extra_examples.fact: The current published Heritage at Risk register is the 2025 annual snapshot.
extra_examples.gate: Recheck material site change/current condition before treating annual HAR status as live acquisition/development evidence.

extra_examples.ref: Heritage at Risk versus development opportunity
extra_examples.fact: HAR inclusion records condition/vulnerability under category-specific criteria.
extra_examples.gate: At-risk status does not prove the asset is available, viable, consentable or suitable for redevelopment.

extra_examples.ref: Registered park geometry versus setting impact
extra_examples.fact: Registered historic parks/gardens have mapped designated areas.
extra_examples.gate: Boundary intersection/proximity is not a complete setting/significance assessment for a proposal.

extra_examples.fact: Registered parks/gardens use grades I, II* and II.
extra_examples.gate: Grade does not itself produce a planning outcome or quantify harm.

extra_examples.fact: Listed building grades classify special interest nationally.
extra_examples.gate: Do not convert Grade I/II*/II directly into a numeric development-success probability without proposal-specific evidence.

extra_examples.fact: Planning Data's scheduled-monument dataset includes some MHCLG-created data pending replacement.
extra_examples.gate: Use Historic England's current legal NHLE entry/full-scale map for exact scheduled extent.

extra_examples.fact: Local heritage lists identify non-designated assets with local significance.
extra_examples.gate: A local list entry must not be treated as a nationally listed building or as requiring Listed Building Consent solely because of local-list status.

extra_examples.fact: A parcel can be affected by multiple distinct heritage designations, local controls, archaeological records and consent regimes.
extra_examples.gate: No promotion until exact canonical parcel geometry is reconciled with current NHLE/LPA/HER evidence and all relevant consent/impact states remain distinct.
